items.title: [experiments] Align Performance experiments with using a shared benchmark harness

labels.name: docs
labels.description: Improvements or additions to the documentation.

items.body:
Merge the per-variant pages from `experiments/perf/` and the original component pages from this PR into a single **Performance** section, driven by a shared variants-aware benchmark harness. Each page picks a variant, or all of them, from a single dropdown, and presents `Last`, `Samples`, `Avg`, `Std dev`, `Min`, and `Max` in one on-page results table.

### Pages

- [`/experiments/performance/tooltip-perf`](https://deploy-preview-3342--base-ui.netlify.app/experiments/performance/tooltip-perf) -- 2000 instances. Variants: Plain buttons, Base UI, Base UI with detached triggers, Radix.
- [`/experiments/performance/triggers-perf`](https://deploy-preview-3342--base-ui.netlify.app/experiments/performance/triggers-perf) -- 500 rows x Dialog/Menu/Popover/Preview Card/Tooltip. Variants: Base UI contained triggers, Base UI detached triggers, Radix (Hover Card stands in for Preview Card). Uses the sidebar `SettingsPanel` to toggle which components render across all variants; changing a toggle resets the results.
- [`/experiments/performance/combobox-perf`](https://deploy-preview-3342--base-ui.netlify.app/experiments/performance/combobox-perf) -- 1000 items, open at mount so the list is part of the measurement. Variants: Base UI with index, Base UI without index, Base UI open API.
- [`/experiments/performance/select-perf`](https://deploy-preview-3342--base-ui.netlify.app/experiments/performance/select-perf) -- 1000 items, open at mount so the list is part of the measurement. Variants: Base UI Select, Radix Select.
- [`/experiments/performance/menu-open-perf`](https://deploy-preview-3342--base-ui.netlify.app/experiments/performance/menu-open-perf) -- times opening an already mounted Menu with 50 items, through a `Menu.createHandle()` handle. Ported from master's `perf/menu-open.tsx` onto the shared harness.

Combobox and Select use `defaultOpen` on the Root because closed popups are lazily mounted -- without it the harness only measures the trigger, not the 1000-item list. The Base UI Select is `modal={false}` and the Combobox lists use `collisionAvoidance={{ side: 'none' }}`, so the open popups neither trap focus nor cover the harness controls.

### Shared harness

The harness in `performance/utils/benchmark.tsx` keeps the existing MutationObserver + 32 ms quiet-window measurement and IQR-based outlier removal, but now:

- Accepts a `variants: { key, label, render, interact? }[]` prop and tracks per-variant samples.
- Provides `Re-render`, `Run 10`, `Run 20`, `Run 50`, `Remove outliers`, and `Reset` controls. The "All variants" option runs each variant in turn and fills the whole table. The picker is hidden when a page has a single variant.
- Renders nothing until `Re-render` or a `Run` button is pressed. Selecting a variant only clears the one on screen.
- Replaces the controls with a "Running <variant> <n> times" status while measuring. The controls keep their space, so the table does not move.
- For variants with `interact`, mounts the variant untimed, waits for the DOM to settle, then times the interaction until the DOM settles again.
- Observes the whole document, since variants portal their popups to `body`, ignoring its own controls and the Next.js dev overlay. Runs cancelled by unmounting, a workload change, or a 10 s timeout record nothing.
- Surfaces stats in an on-page table (one row per variant) and still logs raw arrays to the console for tooling.

Covered by jsdom tests in `docs/src/utils/benchmark.test.tsx`.

### Removed (folded into the above)

- `experiments/perf/{contained,detached,radix}-triggers.tsx` -> covered by `triggers-perf` variants.
- `experiments/perf/menu-open.tsx` -> moved to `performance/menu-open-perf.tsx`.
- `experiments/perf/utils/benchmark.tsx` -> moved under `performance/utils/`. `wait.ts` is deleted; nothing uses it any more.
- `experiments/menu/perf-{contained,detached}.tsx` -> covered by `triggers-perf` with the Menu-only toggle.
- The per-page CSS modules -> merged into a single `performance.module.css`.

Not carried over: the "Measure unmount" toggle of the old trigger pages.

items.title: [field] Move field registration into Field.Root

labels.name: type: enhancement
labels.description: It’s an improvement, but we can’t make up our mind whether it's a bug fix or a new feature.

labels.name: component: field
labels.description: Changes related to the field component.

labels.name: scope: all components
labels.description: Widespread work has an impact on almost all components.

items.body:
This moves field registration ownership into `Field.Root` so field-aware controls only publish lightweight control descriptors through the field context.

The main tradeoff is that `Field` itself gets a bit bigger because it now owns the optional Base UI form-integration path. That is intentional: consumers who use controls like `Select`, `Slider`, `Checkbox`, `Switch`, `RadioGroup`, `Combobox`, and `NumberField` without Base UI `Field`/`Form` no longer pay for that registration logic by default.

The package-level bundle bot still reports a small increase for `@base-ui/react` because the root barrel exports `Field`, which now owns the shared registration path. That root-package number is a noisy aggregate for this change, and the more useful read is:

- `Field` itself got bigger because it now owns registration work that used to live in each control.
- The field-aware controls got smaller because they stopped each carrying that logic themselves.
- When `Field` is bundled together with those controls, the net effect is still smaller overall because the shared Field-owned path deduplicates better than the old per-control setup.

## Changes

- Move form registration out of each control and into `Field.Root` via `useFieldControlRegistration`.
- Add `useRegisterFieldControl` so the controls share one small registration publisher instead of repeating the same effect boilerplate.
- Remove the intermediate registration state hop in `Field.Root` and keep the active control registration in a ref-backed path.
- Preserve submit-time value normalization for controls that need it, including `Select`, `Combobox`, `Field.Control`, and unselected `RadioGroup`.
- Add a regression test for unselected `RadioGroup` values submitted through `Form.onFormSubmit`.
- Simplify the shared registration path so only the long-lived registry callbacks keep stable identity.

## Bundle impact

Bundle bot for the root barrel currently reports `@base-ui/react` at `+630 B` parsed and `+99 B` gzip.

Local bundle-size snapshot diff against fresh `upstream/master` for the narrower entrypoints affected by this refactor:

The last two rows below are real synthetic-bundle measurements where those entrypoint source files are imported together, rather than sums of the individual deltas.

| Entry | Parsed delta | Gzip delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `Field` | `+890 B` | `+194 B` |
| `Checkbox` | `-414 B` | `-154 B` |
| `CheckboxGroup` | `-482 B` | `-171 B` |
| `Combobox` | `-504 B` | `-175 B` |
| `NumberField` | `-418 B` | `-111 B` |
| `RadioGroup` | `-424 B` | `-159 B` |
| `Select` | `-503 B` | `-158 B` |
| `Slider` | `-452 B` | `-168 B` |
| `Switch` | `-445 B` | `-191 B` |
| Synthetic bundle: field-aware controls together | `-738 B` | `-270 B` |
| Synthetic bundle: field-aware controls + `Field` | `+541 B` | `+85 B` |

## Benchmark impact

Chromium production benchmark against `upstream/master` after removing the extra `Field.Root` registration state hop:

| Scenario | Master | This branch | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `Slider x400` without `Field` | `8.2 ms` | `7.3 ms` | `-0.9 ms` |
| `Slider x400` with `Field` | `12.8 ms` | `13.2 ms` | `+0.4 ms` |
| `Select x250` without `Field` | `22.4 ms` | `19.7 ms` | `-2.7 ms` |
| `Select x250` with `Field` | `30.2 ms` | `32.7 ms` | `+2.5 ms` |

So the final shape is:

- Controls used without `Field` are faster and slimmer.
- Wrapped cases are much closer to baseline after removing the extra registration state hop in `Field.Root`.
- The remaining runtime tradeoff is concentrated in the optional `Field` path rather than paid by every field-aware control by default.

items.title: @base-ui/react/input (Field.Control) re-renders on every keystroke even when used uncontrolled (e.g. React Hook Form register)

labels.name: component: field
labels.description: Changes related to the field component.

items.body:
# Get help
Summary


Base UI Input (which renders Field.Control) triggers React state updates on each keystroke (setDirty, setFilled), causing the input component/subtree to re-render continuously while typing. This happens even when the input is used in an uncontrolled way via React Hook Form register.

This makes Base UI Input hard to use in performance-sensitive forms, because RHF’s usual “uncontrolled input = minimal rerenders” benefit is lost.

Expected behavior


When using an uncontrolled input (no value prop, only ref/onChange/onBlur from RHF register), typing should not force React re-renders of the input subtree on every keystroke unless the consumer explicitly opts into controlled state or subscriptions.

Actual behavior


Typing into Base UI Input triggers re-renders on every keystroke.

## Ask a question

Request / questions

1. Is there an intended way to use Base UI Input in a mode that avoids per-keystroke React state updates (and therefore avoids re-rendering the control)?

2. Would you consider an opt-out for tracking dirty/filled/focused state (e.g. trackDirty, trackFilled, trackFocus) for integrations where an external form library owns state/validation?

3. Alternatively, could Field.Control avoid updating React state on each input event and instead update some of this state on blur/commit, or compute it from DOM without setting state?
